title: SLO Activation Lightweight Play Pattern — 30d Pilot
summary: Compact cross-functional plan to trial a repeatable lightweight SLO activation pattern across hosted API and Dedicated pools during a 30-day pilot. Focus is observability alignment, alert noise reduction, and automation for safe rollouts and automated fallbacks.
why_now: Recent capacity incidents exposed mismatches between telemetry signals and escalation policies. Customers are asking for clearer operational guarantees and graceful fallbacks when Dedicated capacity is constrained. We need a pragmatic pattern we can replicate across ~20 services next quarter.
primary_objective: Ship and validate a conservative SLO template and activation workflow that 80% of pilot services adopt within 30 days.
secondary_objectives: Cut false-positive pages by at least 30% for pilot services and deliver a short runnable rollout checklist and automation snippets for canary-based rollouts and fallbacks.
scope: Design SLO template (latency, errors, simple quality guardrail), extract SLIs, build minimal dashboards, craft alerting/paging composite rules, create canary automation and fallback policy, run 3 experiments in staging, run two cross-team workshops.
out_of_scope: Contractual SLA negotiations with legal/finance, deep changes to serving runtime internals, billing model changes.
stakeholders_roles: Owner: Liam Chen (eng-site-reliability). Platform: Marina Ortega (rollout automation). Serving runtime: Keiko Tanaka (telemetry schema). Product (Hosted API): Priya Singh (acceptance). Customer Success: Jonas Meyer (pilot accounts). Observability: Daniel Park (dashboards/alerts). Security/Compliance: Anika Ruiz (audit review).
30d_milestones: Day 0-3 kickoff and SLO draft. Day 4-10 telemetry pipeline and dashboards for 3 pilots. Day 11-18 staging experiments (latency, cache, model fallback). Day 19-24 refine alerts and runbook; workshop #1. Day 25-28 production canary with fallback. Day 29-30 retrospective and next-step decisions.
experiment_plan: 1) Latency stress: vary context lengths, measure p50/p95, verify prefix caching impact. 2) Cache degradation: reduce KV hit rate on staging pool to test routing fallback. 3) Model-variant fallback: trigger automated switch to quantized variant and run prompt-set QA checks.
sli_slo_template: Latency SLOs per route (example p95 targets: small-chat <250ms, long-gen <400ms), Error SLO 99.9% success over rolling 7d, Quality guardrail: <2% relative drop on canonical prompt-set per deploy window, Burn-rate thresholds for paging.
telemetry_and_dashboards: Priority cards: per-route token throughput and p50/p95 latency, GPU/CPU utilization per pool, error class breakdown with trace links, KV cache hit-rate heatmap, cost-per-token trend, composite SLO health card with burn-rate sparkline.
alerting_and_paging_drafts: P0: 5xx >1% over 5m AND SLO burn >2x -> page SRE. P1: sustained p95 breach 30m AND traffic >threshold -> notify owners. Use composite signals (SLI + infra queueing) to avoid noise. Burn-rate based paging: page at 3x in 1h or sustained >1.5x for 6h.
runbook_fragments: Triage checklist: identify affected routes, confirm SLI degradation, check model-variant fallbacks, inspect pool capacity and KV cache heatmap. Mitigations: trigger fallback, scale pool if allowed, enable read-only degraded mode. Communications: incident Slack channel, incident Confluence page template, CS customer alerts.
rollout_and_automation: Canary policy: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 30m gates. Automation snippet: traffic-weighting script (k8s/internal infra) that runs prompt-set quality checks between steps and aborts if quality SLO crosses threshold. Fallback policy: automated routing to lower-cost variant with TTL and owner notification.
staffing_and_training: Add a model-serving SRE pager shadow for first 6 weeks. Two workshops (2h each): SLO template + runbook walkthrough; post-experiment dry-run and adjustments. Add short oncall playbook card to rotation docs.
communications_plan: Weekly Wed 10am PT sync with Product & Platform. Pilot customer check-in at day 21. Sprint-end exec summary with recommended next-step staffing and program ask.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: alert fatigue -> Mitigation: composite triggers + probationary silence window for new alerts. Risk: quality regressions on quantized fallback -> Mitigation: automated prompt-set checks in canary gating. Risk: cross-team coordination overhead -> Mitigation: RACI and 2-weekly mini-standups until pattern stabilizes.
open_questions: Acceptable p95 targets for long-context generation routes (product to confirm). Can finance support short-term burst capacity for Dedicated pools during pilot? Which canonical prompt-sets to use for Hosted vs Dedicated?

notes_to_self: Keep template conservative to avoid noisy pages. Prioritize repeatable automation; manual handoffs reduce velocity. Expect heavy infra plumbing in week one.
